html:
Wu was a state on the lower Yangtze, around today's Suzhou, in the age of the Zhou dynasty. The map shows it from 1500 BCE, but it enters written history only in the 500s BCE, and it fell in 473 BCE.

Tradition says Wu was founded by Taibo, a Zhou prince who went south and lived among the local people. Its people were probably closer to the non-Chinese peoples of the south; Chinese writers described them as cutting their hair short and tattooing their bodies.

Wu rose fast in the Spring and Autumn period. Under King Helü, with the strategist Sun Tzu said to be among his advisers, Wu crushed the great state of Chu and took its capital in 506 BCE. Wu was famous for its bronze swords. Its neighbour and rival Yue struck back: King Goujian of Yue destroyed Wu in 473 BCE.
